Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary:  Acute undifferentiated febrile illness for 7 days with rigors, night sweats, myalgias, nausea, and fatigue without focal respiratory or urinary symptoms. Recent travel to Vietnam (urban and rural trekking/cycling), returned 4 weeks ago. Took daily malaria prophylaxis (drug unknown). Telehealth visit; in-person examination and labs planned.  
- Relevant differentials (from DDx, consistent with transcript):  
  - Malaria (P. falciparum, P. vivax/ovale) — high likelihood given travel to Vietnam with rural exposure, paroxysmal fevers/sweats, and constitutionals; prophylaxis is not fully protective.  
  - Enteric fever (typhoid/paratyphoid) — medium likelihood with persistent fever and minimal localizing symptoms after SE Asia travel.  
  - Common viral syndrome (e.g., influenza/COVID-19) — medium likelihood; systemic symptoms without focal source; occupational exposure as a nurse.  
  - Additional considerations: Dengue (low–medium; timing less typical), Leptospirosis (low; no clear freshwater exposure).  
- Working diagnosis:  Undifferentiated febrile illness post–recent travel — rule out malaria.  
- Plan:  
  - Same-day in-person evaluation at central clinic for full exam.  
  - Laboratory testing: thick and thin blood films for malaria; inflammatory markers; general blood tests (as per clinician note).  
  - If unable to attend clinic promptly, present to local Emergency Department (A&E) with clinician note.  
  - Patient advised not to work until investigation clarifies cause and condition is stabilized.  
  - Further management contingent on exam and initial test results.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Malaria (High): Recent rural travel in Vietnam with paroxysmal fevers, sweats, myalgias, and nausea; prophylaxis not fully protective; clinician requested malaria films.  
- Enteric fever (Medium): Prolonged fever with minimal localizing symptoms after SE Asia travel and varied food/water exposures.  
- Common viral syndrome (Medium): Systemic febrile illness with myalgias and fatigue; healthcare worker exposure; absence of focal bacterial source.
